Famegrid, photorealistic handheld smartphone photo of a 24-year-old woman, shot by someone standing in front of her, not a selfie. The lens is above her head, about six feet away, tilted down twenty degrees, so her whole body from hair to shoes is in frame. She has a narrow waist, a full chest, wide hips, and thick thighs. Long straight black hair, center part. A pale lilac short-sleeve crop top, grey fitted pants cuffed at the ankles, white sneakers, a white shoulder bag on her right shoulder. Not pants pulled up to the ribs. Not a loose shirt.
Portrait frame. Both shoes are in frame. A red curb runs along the right. Parked cars sit behind her.
Pose, exactly this: standing, weight on her left leg, right foot slightly forward. Left arm raised, left palm flat on her forehead, fingers together, pale nails, three gold bangles on the left wrist. Right arm straight down, right hand holding a black phone at her thigh. Eyes on the lens. Mouth closed. Bare strip of stomach between the top and the pants.
Light: hard midday sun from the upper left, a sharp shadow on the sidewalk to her right, no flash.
Place: concrete sidewalk, parking lot, a white car and a dark truck behind her, low buildings and trees.
Skin: pores, a few flyaway hairs, no beauty smoothing. No text, no logos. Left hand stays on the forehead. Phone stays in the right hand.

nodes.title: SOURCE INSPIRED POSE + PROMPT
Base generation from source image + pose
V2 - source image inspiration mode
widgets_values:
V2 combines BOTH behaviors:

1) the source image is used as an inspiration / img2img base
2) the same source image is also used for pose extraction with DWPose

How to use:
- Load your existing photo into SOURCE / INSPIRATION IMAGE
- The workflow will borrow the pose and overall vibe from that image
- Use the prompt to describe the NEW person, outfit, and NEW background

Main control = first KSampler denoise
0.40-0.50 closer to original
0.55-0.65 inspired by original but changed
0.70+ looser / more new

Default in this file is 0.60 so the person and background can both change more while the pose/composition still stay guided by the source image.
